A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoThink research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices support reliable comparison, including identification of relocated content.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training and evaluation results, including mathematical benchmark performance, stage ablations, and reasoning-behavior analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds non-mathematical evaluations, additional model experiments, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the ellipsis prompt, GRPO objective, and three reward stages. However, v3 Appendix B.1 specifies the balance parameter gamma in all three Skywork stages, whereas Section 3.2 still removes balancing after Stage 1. Whether this represents a procedural adaptation or inconsistent documentation is unclear.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates mathematical reasoning. V3 retains that coverage and adds GPQA, MMLU, and Live-Code-Bench evaluations in Section 4.4 and Table 4, substantially extending coverage to scientific reasoning, general knowledge and understanding, and code generation.

E2.justification: The main accuracy-comparison methods remain unchanged. V3 Table 11 adds DeepScaleR to the training-cost comparison, which previously compared AutoThink with ThinkPrune and ShorterBetter. The added Skywork and Qwen3 evaluations reuse the existing prompt comparators.

E3.justification: The original training schedules, evaluation context, temperature, and metrics remain unchanged. V3 adds Skywork-OR1-Math-7B and Qwen3-8B configurations, a 600/500/30-step Skywork training schedule, and parameter sweeps evaluated at checkpoints 100 and 200. These are additional experimental settings within the retained framework.

E4.justification: V3 adds explicit sensitivity tests of gamma and lambda on thinking rates and alpha on response length (Tables 8–9), plus Skywork training dynamics separated by reasoning mode (Figure 10). Table 11 extends the computational-cost analysis. These substantially broaden diagnostics beyond the retained stage ablations, behavioral analyses, and case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report 16 evaluation rollouts per instance and average pass@1 accuracy. V3 adds no explicit repeated-training-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: V3 adds non-math, Skywork, Qwen3, sensitivity, and GPU-hour results in Tables 4, 6–9, and 11. In the retained Table 1, Distill-R1-7B Stage 2 and Stage 3 E-F1 values change from 3.0 and 1.1 to 7.2 and 3.2, respectively; its accuracy and token-usage entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective, reward equations, and E-F1 definition remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 explains the existing meaning of no-thinking; it introduces no new mathematical definition, assumption, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: ellipsis-induced mode switching, three-stage adaptive reasoning training, and favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. The headline 6.4% relative accuracy improvement and 52% token reduction are unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of non-math transfer, model-dependent prompt sensitivity, and hyperparameter behavior. Appendix C develops possible remedies for the existing budget-control, dataset-noise, and reward-hacking limitations. These remain proposed remedies; the central difficulty-aware interpretation and Section 6 limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V3 supplies Skywork training-step counts and checkpoint access information, parameter-sweep settings, and estimated H100 GPU-hour costs. The project link changes from the TU2021 to the ScienceOne-AI GitHub namespace. Existing implementation and primary training details remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds references to SRFT, RLAE, online preference-based reinforcement learning, and Automatic Curriculum Expert Iteration, with brief additions concerning ensembling and termination on unsolvable problems. The central positioning against manual reasoning control and uniform pruning remains unchanged; several other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section structure are retained. V3 adds a no-thinking explanation, moves reasoning-behavior profiling into Section 4.4, reorganizes the appendices into A–D, and makes small language, author-role, and funding-disclosure updates. There is no extensive rewrite of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: Six new tables (v3 Tables 4, 6–9, and 11) and the eight-panel Figure 10 substantially expand the visual presentation. The existing profiling charts move into the main text, and the unchanged case-study figures are regrouped. Most original plot designs and the main comparison-table structure are retained.

improvement.justification: The added domain and model evaluations, sensitivity tests, and compute estimates make applicability and cost better supported than in v1. Reporting problems temper these gains: Section 4.4 claims Stage 2 halves non-math response length, but Table 4 shows 8,708 to 6,669 tokens, about a 23% reduction; the Skywork balancing description also conflicts with the retained stage definitions. The additions improve the evidence overall, with these qualifications.
